take_homes: An agent grading its own work is soft, so its report is a hypothesis. A cold reader in a fresh task is better, and even that goes soft if I ask the flattering question first.
Turn a session into a rules file, retro it against what really happened, and push back on the charitable verdict. A fresh agent can then repeat the move on someone else's input.
Running the experiment myself gives me felt experience that reading reports doesn't.

monday.move: Take the rules-file-plus-retro move and try it on one non-engineering workflow (sales follow-up emails), with a fresh-session cold read of the output before anyone trusts it
monday.who: me, then one person from sales
monday.stop_condition: The cold read and the sales person's gut disagree with the agent's self-report, and I can't tell which is right
monday.blocker: Nobody in sales has asked for it and I haven't checked who would maintain the rules file.

misconception.why: I thought a good agent meant good output and checking was for beginners. Then the module said the agent's self-check is the same kind of output as the work and goes soft, and the cold-read section showed a second agent going soft too. I'm not convinced I need to check everything myself, but I'll stop treating the agent's own review as a check.

one_line: The look-back and cold-read bits taught me something, but the first half I knew already, and the filler paragraphs between the exercise phases wasted my time.
